title: Codex Roadmap-Review Verdict
description: Structured output for codex roadmap-review agents spawned by /adversarial-review-roadmap. Orchestrator parses this to decide approval vs. another round. Used via `codex exec --output-schema <this file>` per adversarial-review-roadmap.md §Codex Invocation. Distinct from plan-review-verdict.schema.json (single-plan reviews) and review-verdict.schema.json (code-diff reviews).

verdict.description: APPROVE_AS_IS = no critical or important findings; roadmap is implementation-ready (each child plan can be picked up by /adversarial-review-plan). APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES = only important and/or optional findings; author should patch but the runner can begin on the first plan in parallel. REVISE_AND_RESUBMIT = at least one critical finding; another round is required before any child plan starts.

summary.description: One short paragraph (under 200 words) on overall roadmap state. Must state, for round 2+, whether the prior round's findings are resolved and what the single most important remaining concern is (if any).

round_resolution_audit.description: Required in round 2+. One entry per finding raised in the immediately prior round. Each entry cites the prior finding and its resolution status. Use null in round 1.

status.description: RESOLVED = fix is correct and complete. PARTIAL = directionally correct but misses a sub-case. UNRESOLVED = not addressed. NEW_PROBLEM = the fix introduced a different issue that supersedes the original.

justification.description: One sentence citing the roadmap section that addresses or fails to address the prior finding.

findings.description: All findings against the current roadmap draft. Empty array on APPROVE_AS_IS. Each finding tags the dimension it relates to so the author can prioritise and the orchestrator can route surgical edits to the right section.

severity.description: critical = blocks dispatching the affected plan(s); important = should fix before that plan starts but can be patched in parallel with earlier plans; optional = nit or deferrable cleanup.

dimension.description: Which review axis this finding relates to. Used by the orchestrator to apply surgical edits to the correct roadmap section.

where.description: Roadmap section reference (e.g. '§4 Plan 5' or '§5 Coverage map row 3') plus any repo file path + line number the finding implicates (e.g. existing plan files, the upstream spec).

issue.description: One-paragraph explanation of what is wrong, missing, or ambiguous.

suggested_fix.description: Concrete patch the author can apply. Specific enough that the author can act without re-deriving context (e.g. 'split Plan 5 into 5a/5b at the skill-bundle/git-MCP boundary; move repo registry from 5 to 5b').

spec_coverage_audit.description: Audit of the roadmap's §5 Coverage map against the upstream spec, when one exists. Each entry flags either a spec item missing from the map or a map row whose plan attribution is wrong. Null when the roadmap has no upstream spec.

spec_item.description: Spec section or acceptance criterion the audit entry is about (quote or paraphrase).

issue.description: MISSING = spec item not in coverage map and not in any plan. WRONG_PLAN = mapped to a plan that does not actually deliver it. AMBIGUOUS = spec item split across plans without clear ownership. SILENTLY_DROPPED = roadmap omits the item without an explicit out-of-scope entry.

where.description: Spec file path + section, plus the roadmap location that should have addressed it.

cross_plan_coupling_audit.description: Cases where one plan's claimed contract does not match another plan's assumed contract. Distinct from findings[] because these are inter-plan consistency checks rather than per-plan defects. Null or empty array if none.

producing_plan.description: Plan slug or §4 reference that introduces the contract.

consuming_plan.description: Plan slug or §4 reference that depends on the contract.

contract.description: The contract as stated (interface, data shape, file location, etc.).

issue.description: What's inconsistent and how it would manifest if not fixed.

missed_risks.description: Roadmap-level risks not captured in §7. Each item should be actionable (suggest a mitigation or a plan-level rework), not philosophical. Null or empty array if none.

affected_plans.description: Comma-separated plan slugs or '§4 Plan N' refs.
